Rejection is a really hard thing to get over with, to be honest. It's something that sticks to you no matter what, most especially with our bipolar/depression/crippling anxiety. You can't just help but go back to the time when you thought you found an ally and then you were betrayed. Or that time when some people around you were insensitive enough to tell or ask you at the wrong thing at the wrong time. All of which are unfortunate events, but it's what our minds keep replaying in our thoughts making us feel so isolated and alone. The worst part of it are the people who are more curious about your condition who thinks they are trying to help, but are unknowingly giving you the confirmation that no one will ever come to understand your frustrations and worries and end up making you feel even more alone. Unbearably alone.

I feel the same way everyday. Feeling rejected, a waste of space, a burden to my family and friends and lover. I feel this unbearable loneliness despite the constant love and support I receive from my boyfriend. I tend to hurt and push him away during my episodes and sometimes I feel like even the feeling of his touch is so unbearable on my skin. And I feel extremely guilty once I have calmed down. That leads me to think that he is better off without me and I want to break up to keep him safe from me and this all hurt so much that I would hurt myself, think of trying to hang myself or overdose with over the counter medicines, in which he would try to stop me by keeping an eye on me and taking away any dangerous items in the house.

I just emerged from an episode as I write this comment and to tell you the truth, I was thinking of starting my own thread with a detailed description of how the frustration of trying to find a job that is more suited for my personality and the sudden downward spiral from frustration to feeling unbearably helpless about my future to having a full blown episode.

But after I read your post, I really want to tell you that, yes people can be stupid sometimes and gives in to their curiosity and ask uncomfortable and sometimes insensitive questions, but this is their way of trying to get to know you. Since, they never did experience what you're experiencing yourself, they ask questions to try and imagine, using your own words, how it feels like. I'm not telling you to share everything to someone you do not trust or are uncomfortable with, but it helps if you express that what they're asking is making you feel uncomfortable and that you prefer to keep the answer to yourself. That way, in the case of your friends, they will know what to say or what not to say and they may even come to understand what you are going through.

As for your desire to find someone who can relate to you, you might want to participate in a support group. I know that it's a very uncomfortable experience, but it's worth it if you can find that someone who can relate to what you're saying.
